hints: Focus on what functional group each formula really shows, a ketone, an aldehyde or a carboxylic acid.
Recall that alkaline aqueous iodine only gives a yellow precipitate with a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group in a methyl ketone (or ethanal).
Check Tollens' reagent next, it oxidises aldehydes only, then decide if ethanoic acid can behave like a methyl ketone.
walkthrough:
**Identify X, Y and Z**

Great start, let's name what we have. X is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$, which is butan-2-one, a ketone.

Y is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$, which is propanal, an aldehyde. Z is $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, which is ethanoic acid, a carboxylic acid.

**Test statement 1 with the iodoform test**

The iodoform test with alkaline aqueous iodine gives $\text{CHI}_3$ (yellow precipitate) with methyl ketones containing $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COR} + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{RCO}_2\text{Na} + 3\text{NaI} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

X has $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so statement 1 is correct.

**Test statement 2 with Tollens' reagent**

Tollens' reagent, $\text{[Ag(NH}_3\text{)}_2\text{]}^+$, is a mild oxidising agent that oxidises aldehydes to carboxylic acids, forming a silver mirror.

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CHO} + 2\text{[Ag(NH}_3\text{)}_2\text{]}^+ + 3\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CO}_2^- + 2\text{Ag} + 4\text{NH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Y is an aldehyde, so statement 2 is correct.

**Test statement 3, does the acid give iodoform?**

Z does contain $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$, but it is part of a carboxylic acid, not a methyl ketone or ethanal. Carboxylic acids do not undergo the tri-iodination and cleavage step.

So Z does not react, which means statement 3 is correct. All three statements are correct.

options.A: Correct. Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. X is a methyl ketone so gives iodoform, Y is an aldehyde so gives a silver mirror with Tollens', and Z is a carboxylic acid so does not give iodoform.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination (1 and 2 only) misses that statement 3 is also true. Students choose this if they think any $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, including in $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, gives a positive iodoform test.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination (2 and 3 only) wrongly rejects statement 1. Students choose this if they forget that ketones with a methyl group directly attached to C=O, like $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$, are positive in the iodoform test.
options.D: Incorrect. This combination (1 only) wrongly rejects statement 2. Students choose this if they confuse Tollens' reagent, which tests for aldehydes, with Fehling's conditions or think only methanal reacts.
